english_classification.chapter_title: Concerning the Four Great Days that have come forth from one another, together with the Four Nights
english_classification.chapter_note: The oldest teaching layer is dominant. A four-fold day/night schema maps cosmic entities to twelve-hour structures. The substrate is clean through the first three positions of each sequence. The fourth positions (day 4 = Jesus the Splendour, night 4 = law of Sin) show editorial bridging toward institutional identifications ('his church,' 'the twelve sects,' 'the old man'). This is a classic pattern: the editor extends a complete cosmic schema into the contemporary world at the terminal position. The substrate pentadic structure (five elements, five sense organs, five spirits) underlies the twelve-fold systematization, which Gardner rightly notes is 'secondary' — yet the cosmic correspondences within each position (zodiacal signs as Matter's thrones, five parts above/below, heat and cold as father and mother) are genuinely substratic. Editorial fatigue is moderate: substrate vocabulary drops from 34.09 to 8.62 in the second half while editorial_bridge rises from 0.0 to 2.39.
